summary.intent: Triage and fix findings from a crypto-focused code review of a CipherBox SDK phase (folder createSubfolder error-path zeroization), applying only in-domain, safe fixes and discarding out-of-scope or design-judgment findings.
summary.outcome: Fixed a LOW finding by widening the try block in registration.ts so TEE-wrap key generation throws also trigger key zeroization, fixed a stale provenance comment in encoding.ts, added a focused regression test locking the new zeroization path, verified with typecheck and full sdk-core test suite (392 passing), and committed the changes.

repo: sdk-core error-path key zeroization pattern (established in file/index.ts): the try block should start immediately after key generation/minting, not after early validation, so every post-mint throw path zeroes the keys.

packages/sdk/src/client.ts's sharedFile* codecs are pre-existing from phase 68.2-08 and handle a distinct web↔sdk hex/base64 boundary — deduping them into crypto's codecs is legitimate cleanup but out of scope for a phase-77 diff.
wrap.ts's 1:1 passthrough is a deliberate D-09 seam with an existing test, not dead code — do not 'simplify' it away.

code.finding: Early validation throws (lines ~88/93) and the TEE-wrap block originally sat outside the try, so a malformed TEE pubkey throwing in hexToBytes leaked the 3 minted keys; try boundary moved to start right after key generation.

The @cipherbox/crypto mock omitted hexToBytes/bytesToHex/wrapIpnsKeyForTee, so a naive teeKeys-throw test would fail for the wrong reason (undefined fn); had to add these to the mock to faithfully test the TEE-wrap-throw zeroization path.
Contained a stale provenance comment left over from the phase's new file; removed/updated it as it was in the phase's own diff.

workflow: When triaging code-review output, findings squarely in the phase's stated domain (even if not explicitly called out) are worth fixing proactively (e.g. the early-validation throw paths alongside the reported TEE-wrap leak).

Verify agent-reported review findings against the actual code (grep import/call sites) before trusting their framing — an agent can be right about the underlying issue while wrong about a supporting detail (e.g. claiming client.ts already imports codecs it doesn't).

After a review-driven fix that changes behavior (even strictly-additive), typecheck + run the specific affected test file before considering it safe, then add a targeted regression test to lock the fix rather than relying on existing coverage alone.

friction: Simplify-agent finding on client.ts dedup was partially inaccurate (claimed existing imports that didn't exist), requiring manual grep verification before deciding to discard it.
Test mocks for @cipherbox/crypto were incomplete (missing hexToBytes/bytesToHex/wrapIpnsKeyForTee), adding extra investigation overhead to write a correct regression test for the zeroization fix.
open_items: client.ts sharedFile* codec dedup with crypto package's codecs was identified as valid low-value cleanup but deliberately deferred as out-of-scope (pre-existing, untouched file, phase 68.2-08 code).
